value.name: lays out records for comparison
value.description: Asha places the Hatcher trial record and the clerk's intake log on Whitfield's blotter so the stamped times can be compared side by side.
evidence: laid the Hatcher trial record and the clerk's intake log on his blotter so the four-eighteen stamp sat above her own five-oh-six in the same line of sight

value.name: corrects the stamp order
value.description: Asha explicitly corrects her earlier mistake about the order of the stamps before the committee meets.
evidence: "The stamp is four-eighteen," she said. "I was wrong about the order this morning, and I'm correcting it before the committee sits."

value.name: Whitfield silently reviews the intake page
value.description: Whitfield draws the intake page closer and reads it without immediately responding to Asha.
evidence: Whitfield did not answer at once; he drew the intake page an inch closer with two fingers and read it without lifting his head

value.name: Asha holds her ground
value.description: Asha remains standing, silent and attentive, while Whitfield reads the documents.
evidence: Asha stood where she was and let him
Asha did not sit, and she did not speak. She kept her hands at her sides and her eyes on Whitfield while he read

value.name: Whitfield compares the records silently
value.description: Whitfield turns the intake page slightly and compares it to Asha's handwritten line without offering approval or criticism.
evidence: Whitfield turned the intake page a quarter inch with the pad of his index finger, compared it without comment to the line she had written in her own hand, and let his breath out through his nose in a way that was neither agreement nor reproach

value.name: Asha endures the silence
value.description: Asha deliberately stays quiet in the tense office, choosing not to soften her correction with further explanation.
evidence: The office was quiet enough that she could hear the radiator tick once behind his chair, and she made herself stand inside that quiet rather than fill it, because anything she said now would only soften a correction she had come here to make hard

value.name: Whitfield rereads without responding
value.description: Whitfield reads the intake page again in silence while Asha maintains her steady, confrontational stance.
evidence: He read the intake page a second time without speaking, and she stood inside the quiet she had made and let it press against him rather than against her

value.name: Asha prepares to move
value.description: After a long silence, Asha begins to shift her stance, signaling the scene is about to change.
